sodium nucleinate is a new, highly effective immunomodulator with a broad spectrum of activity.
the low molecular RNA preparations of the nucleic acids (sodium nucleinate and RNA 4S) increase the nonspecific resistance of mice and rats to conditionally pathogen and pathogenic micro-organisms.

the mechanism of action of the low molecular RNA of rat liver (4 S) and sodium nucleinate.
the problem of the non-specific stimulation of the macroorganism resistance.
the study of the mechanism of action of the preparation sodium nucleinate.

sodium nucleinate is a highly effective immunomodulatory preparation.
the preparation has a stimulating activity on the nonspecific resistance of the organism and does not affect the formation of post-infection immunity.
the preparation sodium nucleinate has a pronounced non-specific stimulating activity, and it can be used in the therapy of the infectious diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RNA of the rat's liver (4S), the RNA of the calf thymus and the RNA of the yeast (3S) are not immunostimulants and sodium nucleinate is the only RNA preparation which has the stimulating activity in the non-specific immunity.
the RNA of the nucleinate is the low molecular RNA, which has a pronounced stimulating effect on nonspecific resistance.
the preparation is a low-molecular RNA, the activity of which is not connected with its molecular weight.

sodium nucleinate is effective in the treatment of infections of various aetiology and that the preparation can be used as an immunomodulator.
